raw_response:
I’m 67 this year. I never went to school, but I’ve been farming these 33 mu for 45 years — since I was a young bride. It’s just me and my old man now. Our children left for the city. We keep 28 mu in wheat and maize, back to back, and 5 mu in cotton on the east side. Cotton is murder on the back with all the picking, but the money is better than maize if the trader gives a fair price.

For wheat, I always sow around October 10th, after the National Day holiday. I use my own seed — I’ve been saving it forever. It’s not the fancy kind from the shop, but it knows this dirt. Before sowing, I spread one big bag of compound fertilizer on each mu — the kind they write three 15s on. I don’t know what those numbers mean exactly, but the shopkeeper says it’s good, and my wheat always looks fine. Then at Qingming, when the wheat starts jointing, if it looks a bit yellow I throw half a bag of urea on top. That’s my rule — one bag compound, half bag urea. I water three times: once before winter so the seedlings don’t freeze-dry, once at jointing, and once when the grain is filling. Water costs a lot now — they meter the well — but I’d rather spend the money than cry over empty bins. I spray herbicide once, and if I see aphids I spray insecticide. We hire the combine for harvest in early June. We’re too old to cut wheat by hand anymore. If the spring rain is decent, I expect about 900 jin per mu.

Then there’s no rest — maize goes in that same week, around June 15th. I buy hybrid seed from the shop, about 3 jin per mu. You can’t save hybrid seed; I learned that the hard way years ago. We hire the neighbor’s tractor to till quick after the wheat straw comes off, then plant. I put down one bag of compound per mu, all at once in the hole — no time for fussing when the heat is coming and the clock is ticking. If it doesn’t rain by mid-July, I irrigate once when the plants are knee-high. Usually that’s enough. I spray herbicide. Harvest is end of September, hire the machine again. Should get about 1,000 jin per mu if the summer rains behave.

Cotton goes in around April 20th. I use local seed. One bag of compound per mu at planting. Cotton needs more medicine — those bollworms are devils. I spray insecticide three, maybe four times through the summer. I irrigate twice if it’s dry, once at flowering and once when the bolls are swelling. The killing part is picking — September through October, three or four rounds. With just two old people, we hire pickers from the village. It costs 150 yuan a day or more, but what can you do? The cotton won’t pick itself. I hope for about 500 jin of seed cotton per mu, though last year was a bit less.

Money is always tight. We need close to 24,000 yuan for all the inputs, maybe more if picking goes long. I have to balance it in my head — if I buy extra fertilizer for wheat, I might not have cash for cotton pickers. But I learned 30 years ago: don’t cheap out on wheat fertilizer. A bad wheat year means borrowing money for the whole winter, and the interest kills you. Better to spend a little more and sleep easy.
